## Summary

Implemented the GPU-side "height→normal live" capability in full; found the app-wiring half of the brief rests on a false premise and documented that honestly instead of fabricating state.

**Built** (gates run by the dragon, not me — Bash was restricted to read-only lookups):
- `crates/umber-gpu/src/shaders.rs`: `PaintParams` grown 32→48 bytes (`height_strength` field), new binding 12 `height_tex`, new `height_perturbed_normal()` using the Mikkelsen (2010) screen-space surface-gradient technique (no TBN needed), wired into `shade()` behind `PAINT_HAS_HEIGHT_TEXTURE`.
- `crates/umber-gpu/src/renderer.rs`: matching Rust `PaintParams`, `MeshPaint.height_view`, bind-group-layout binding 12, `MeshBuffers::set_height_texture`/`clear_height_texture`. Caught and fixed a clobber bug before it shipped — base color is re-bound unconditionally every frame, so a naive height setter would get wiped next frame; fixed with a `write_paint_params` composer over `bound_paint ∪ bound_height`. Added 2 new golden tests + 4 helpers, with a full hand/formula derivation in the test doc comment.
- `crates/umber-gpu/src/view_mode.rs`, `crates/umber-app/src/viewport.rs`: doc-only updates recording the new capability and its boundary.
- `docs/specs/requirements.md` §5, `docs/loop/kill-reports/2026-10-12-height-normal.md`: written.

**Deferred, not faked**: the brief wanted `viewport.rs` to bind height "when the active channel is Height." I checked — that state doesn't exist. `PaintState` has one `PaintTarget` per tile (base color only), `ChannelKind` is just `Color|Data` (no `Height` variant), and `document.rs` itself already documents per-channel GPU binding as a future "tile pool" slice. Per CLAUDE.md's "don't invent a new global," I left `set_height_texture` built and tested but app-uncalled, and recorded the gap in three places (kill report, `viewport.rs` doc, `requirements.md`).

**Unverified**: `dpdx`/`dpdy`/`sign` WGSL builtins have zero prior use in this codebase and no vendored naga reference to check against — I'm relying on spec knowledge, not a GPU run (session couldn't run `cargo test`). Flagged explicitly in the kill report.
